subject: english-literature
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the assessment objectives.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Imagery that appeals to the senses (sight, sound, touch) is used by poets mainly to...
options: Make experiences vivid and draw the reader into the poem's world
questions.explain: Sensory imagery immerses the reader, making emotions and scenes feel concrete and immediate.

questions.q: A poem of fourteen lines, often in iambic pentameter with a turn in argument, is most likely a...
questions.explain: The fourteen-line form with a volta is the defining feature of a sonnet.

questions.q: When a poem about 'memory' moves between past and present tense, this often...
options: Means the poem is a ballad
Blurs the boundary between then and now, showing how the past persists
questions.explain: Shifting tense can dramatise how memory intrudes on the present, keeping the past emotionally alive.

questions.q: Which pig acts as Napoleon's propagandist, persuading the animals to accept his decisions?
questions.explain: Squealer twists facts and rewrites events to justify Napoleon's rule.

questions.q: The most analytical response to a striking image in an unseen poem is to...
options: Skip it because it is unseen
State that the poet 'uses imagery' and move on
Name the device, explore its effect, and link it to the poem's theme
questions.explain: Naming a method is only the start; exploring its effect and connecting it to meaning is what earns higher marks.

questions.q: Which Soviet leaders are Napoleon and Snowball generally taken to represent?
questions.explain: Napoleon represents Stalin and Snowball represents Trotsky, who was driven into exile.

questions.q: How does Napoleon finally seize sole power over the farm?
options: He sets his trained dogs on Snowball to chase him away
questions.explain: Napoleon unleashes the fierce dogs he reared in secret to expel Snowball.

questions.q: Animal Farm is an allegory for which historical event?
questions.explain: Orwell's fable allegorises the Russian Revolution and the rise of Stalinist tyranny.

questions.q: A poem spoken in the voice of a single fictional speaker, revealing their character to a silent listener, is a...
questions.explain: A dramatic monologue uses one speaker's voice to expose their personality, often unintentionally, to an implied listener.

questions.q: What is the original final commandment, "All animals are equal", changed to?
options: "All animals are equal, but some animals are more equal than others"
questions.explain: The corrupted commandment exposes the pigs' hypocrisy and the betrayal of the revolution's ideals.

questions.q: If a poem's lines follow the pattern da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM, the metre is...
questions.explain: Five iambic feet per line is iambic pentameter, the most common metre in English poetry.

questions.q: When a poem about 'loss' uses the present tense to describe a person now gone, the effect is often to...
options: Confuse the reader for no reason
Keep the memory vivid and immediate, as if the person is still present
Prove the poem is a sonnet
questions.explain: Present tense can make memory feel alive and ongoing, emphasising how loss keeps the absent person emotionally present.
